topics.name: Photosynthesis and respiration
subtopics: Photosynthesis: plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight to produce glucose, releasing oxygen (word equation)
Plants change glucose into starch, cellulose and other compounds
Respiration: energy is released from food in all living organisms (word equation)

topics.name: Interactions and interdependence within the environment
subtopics: Ecology and levels of study: populations, communities, ecosystems and the biosphere
Ecosystems: biotic and abiotic components; habitats and adaptation to change
Feeding relationships: producers, consumers (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores) and decomposers
Energy flow in food chains and food webs; trophic levels and energy loss
Balance in an ecosystem and disruption by natural and human factors
Adaptations: structural, functional and behavioural; extinction
Conservation of ecosystems by environmentalists and individuals

topics.name: Micro-organisms
subtopics: Types of micro-organisms: viruses, bacteria, protista and fungi
Harmful micro-organisms and diseases (TB, AIDS, malaria, cholera); preventing their spread
Useful micro-organisms: decomposition and use in food (yoghurt) and medicine (penicillin)

topics.name: Introduction to the Periodic Table of Elements
subtopics: The Periodic Table as a classification system devised by Mendeleev; metals, semi-metals and non-metals
Each element has a name, symbol, atomic number and position
Properties of metals, semi-metals and non-metals

topics.name: Atoms
subtopics: Atoms are the building blocks of matter; elements consist of one kind of atom
Sub-atomic particles: protons and neutrons in the nucleus, electrons around it; atoms are neutral
Pure substances: elements (including diatomic molecules) and compounds
Compounds form by chemical reactions with atoms in fixed ratios; decomposition by heating or electrolysis
Mixtures of elements and compounds are separated by physical means

topics.name: Particle model of matter
subtopics: All matter is made of particles with empty space between them
Arrangement, movement and forces of particles in solids, liquids and gases
Diffusion in liquids and gases
Change of state explained by the particle model
Density, mass and volume; density of different states and materials; floating and sinking
Expansion and contraction when heated and cooled
Gas pressure caused by collisions of particles

topics.name: Chemical reactions
subtopics: Reactants and products; re-arrangement of atoms; breaking and forming of bonds
Indigenous knowledge examples of useful chemical reactions such as fermentation in brewing

topics.name: Static electricity
subtopics: Friction transfers electrons between materials, causing positive and negative charges
Like charges repel and unlike charges attract
Discharge causes sparks or shocks of static electricity

topics.name: Energy transfer in electrical systems
subtopics: A circuit is a system for transferring electrical energy; closed circuits
Components: conducting wires, switches, cells/batteries and resistors
Electric current as the flow of charges; resistors influence current and can provide useful heat and light
Effects of current: heating (bulb filaments, fuses, short circuits), magnetic (electromagnets) and chemical (electrolysis)

topics.name: Series and parallel circuits
subtopics: Series circuits: one pathway; adding resistors in series decreases the current
Parallel circuits: two or more pathways; adding resistors in parallel increases the overall current

topics.name: Visible light
subtopics: Light is emitted by luminous objects, travels in straight lines at 300 000 km/s
The spectrum of visible light; rainbows through refraction and dispersion
Opaque and transparent substances; shadows
Absorption of light and the colour of objects
Reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection; smooth and rough surfaces
Seeing light: receptor cells in the retina and nerve impulses to the brain
Refraction by transparent substances, prisms and lenses

topics.name: The Solar System
subtopics: The Sun is a star producing heat and light through nuclear reactions (hydrogen to helium)
Objects orbiting the Sun: planets and moons, asteroids, dwarf planets, Kuiper Belt, Oort Cloud and comets
Gravity keeps objects in stable orbits; the Solar System is disc-shaped
Earth’s position as third planet and the conditions that support life

topics.name: Beyond the Solar System
subtopics: The Milky Way Galaxy: a spiral galaxy of billions of stars held together by gravity
The nearest stars: the Sun and Alpha Centauri
Light years, light hours and light minutes as measures of distance
Billions of galaxies beyond the Milky Way; size of the observable Universe

topics.name: Looking into space
subtopics: Early viewing of space; constellations and their cultural stories
Optical telescopes (SALT, Hubble) and radio telescopes (SKA)
Good viewing conditions and South African observation locations
